Brief for fix-cursor: the suspected Windows hook defect, what to establish before touching code, and the traps the droid fix (PR #2349) hit. Read this whole thing before editing — the first section is a stop condition.

## Establish the evidence FIRST. Do not change the gate until you have it.

The claim is a suspicion, not a diagnosis. `cursor/hooks.go:124-132` says Cursor spawns hook commands through the native OS shell (cmd.exe on Windows). If that is true, then the sh wrapper cannot work there *whether or not sh exists*: cmd strips the outer quotes (special characters present, so it takes the "otherwise" branch of its quote rule), `>/dev/null` becomes a cmd redirection to a nonexistent path, and the statement dies before sh is reached. `agent.UseWindowsProductionHooks`'s probe runs `sh -c 'exit 0'`, which carries no cmd metacharacters, so it reports success on any host with Git Bash and keeps the broken wrapper — the exact hole the droid fix closed with `agent.HookHostIsWindows()`.

But nobody has read cursor's runner. Establish it the way droid's was:
- Read the SHIPPED binary, per-platform. The platform branch is folded at build time, so download the Windows build specifically and strings-grep its bundle for the spawn call; do not infer Windows behaviour from the mac build. Record the exact composition (`/C "H"` quoted? `/d /s /c` with the command appended verbatim? `%ComSpec%`?) and check it across several versions, because droid changed its composition three times.
- **Which runner even matters on Windows is an open question, and it is the first thing to settle.** `.cursor/hooks.json` is read by both Cursor IDE and the `cursor-agent` CLI (our e2e driver runs binary `agent`, e2e/agents/cursor_cli.go:35). Issue #1424's reporter was on the IDE. If both exist on Windows the wrapper has to work under both, since one file serves both.
- If the evidence says cursor resolves a shell itself after all, STOP and write that down — a confirmed "not a bug" is a good outcome here, and the droid PR's doc comment now points at exactly this investigation.

## The strongest existing lead

Issue #1424 ("Cursor hooks not firing on Windows 11") was closed by #1735, whose resolution comment says cursor "now installs a native cmd.exe wrapper **when no sh is present** (probe-gated, so it's a no-op where sh works)". The reporter's environment was **Windows 11 + Git Bash (MINGW64)** — sh present. So under the shipped fix that user gets the sh wrapper, and if cursor goes through cmd.exe they are still broken today. The comment asks for a retest confirmation and none was ever posted. Read #1424 and #1735 before you start; that is your reproduction case.

## The change, if the evidence supports it

`cursor/hooks.go:133`, `agent.UseWindowsProductionHooks(ctx)` → `agent.HookHostIsWindows()`, and rewrite the comment at 124-132 to say what you actually established. Migration needs no new code: `syncEntireHook` (line 144-164) already replaces a managed hook whose command is not the wanted one, and `agent.IsManagedHookCommand` recognises both Windows shapes — droid relied on exactly that.

Do NOT touch codex's gate in this PR. Codex demonstrably passes the Windows nightly with the sh wrapper installed, so it has evidence cursor lacks; and one objective per PR.

## Test blast radius — this is where cursor is harder than droid

Four things in `cursor/hooks_test.go` that droid did not have:

1. `TestInstallHooks_WindowsProbeSuccessKeepsShWrappers` (line 72) **asserts the very behaviour you would be removing**. It has to be inverted or deleted, not worked around — and it matches ci.yml's `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'` filter, so it runs on the Windows job.
2. `TestInstallHooks_WindowsProbeFlipMigratesCleanly` (129) loses its premise once the probe no longer decides anything. Rework it into an sh→cmd migration test; droid's `TestInstallHooks_WindowsMigratesShWrappers` is the model, including the per-hook-type count assertion that catches a stale entry left beside the new one (two entries double-fire).
3. Host-hardcoded sh expectations at lines 61-66, 92-93, 348, 355, 444 will fail on a Windows host against an install that no longer writes them. Key them to the host the way droid's commit 96bd59fd7 did (`droidHookCommand` / `droidStopHookCommand`). **Keep one helper that does NOT delegate** — droid's `droidWindowsHookCommand` states the literal `"entire hooks cursor " + verb` and calls the Windows wrapper outright, and that is the only thing pinning the prefix and every verb; the delegating helpers assert the implementation against itself. Collapsing the two later looks like removing duplication and silently deletes the real assertion.
4. `TestCommittedDogfoodHooksIsCurrent` (619) checks this repo's committed `.cursor/hooks.json`, which holds the **sh** form. On a Windows host it will fail once the gate is host-only, because a committed file can only carry one form. Decide that deliberately — skip on Windows, or accept "run the suite on Linux" — and say which in the PR. Note codex already has this condition latent for the same reason.

Also: `TestUseWindowsProductionHooks` in the agent package has a "windows with working sh keeps sh wrappers" case. That stays valid for codex — do not delete it.

## Pin the composition before merge, in CI

`cmd/entire/cli/agent/hook_command_exec_windows_test.go` executes wrappers for real, is Windows-only, and runs on ci.yml's windows job under the `(Windows|MSYS)` filter. Add a cursor-shaped runner there modelled on the composition you read out of the binary — that is what turned droid's hand-verification into a pre-merge check (`TestWindowsWrappers_DroidComposition`, and `runDroidWrapper` beside `runWindowsWrapper`, sharing one body). If cursor's composition turns out to be identical to codex's `cmd /C "H"`, say so and reuse `runWindowsWrapper` rather than adding a near-duplicate.

There is no Windows e2e for cursor to lean on: it is excluded from the nightly matrix because its driver drives every prompt through tmux and there is no tmux on Windows, and its headless `-p` mode fires no hooks (nightly-e2e.yml:163-165). So your evidence is binary-reading + the exec test + a manual run, and the PR must not imply e2e coverage it does not have.

## Traps that cost the droid PR real time

- **Never verify lint with `--new-from-rev`.** `maintidx` and `gocyclo` anchor on the `func` signature line, so growing a body — a comment counts, maintidx's LOC term includes them — fails CI on a line the diff never touched, and the baseline hides it. Neither `mise-tasks/lint/go` nor CI's golangci-lint-action applies a baseline. Run the mise-installed 2.11.3 binary directly on the full package set; CI went red on exactly this after a 12-line comment pushed `InstallHooks` to MI 19 against a threshold of 20. The fix was to lift the wrapper construction into small helpers, which also carried the explanation to where it belongs.
- **Windows-only tests need `t.Cleanup(osroot.ResetShared)` registered after `t.TempDir()`** — Windows cannot remove a directory while an `os.Root` handle is open, and Cleanup is LIFO. Cursor's existing Windows tests already do this; copy the comment with it.
- **Name any new test so `(Windows|MSYS)` matches it**, or the Windows job silently skips it. That filter is why cursor's host-hardcoded expectations above have never failed in CI.
- **Do not assert in a doc comment what you have not verified.** The single most valuable review finding on the droid PR was a sentence claiming other agents' runners "resolve a shell themselves", which the repo's own comments contradicted. Write what your evidence supports and name the evidence.
- **Say what does not migrate.** Cursor implements no `HookFreshness`, so `entire status` and `doctor` will not report the stale sh wrapper and `AreHooksInstalled` still answers true for it. An already-enabled Windows repo keeps broken hooks until someone re-runs `entire enable`. Put that in the PR body; a `HookFreshness` for cursor is the durable fix and belongs in its own change.

Reply with what you find about the runner before you start editing, and I will review the PR when it is up.

The report was three independent Windows breakages stacked together, all addressed:

1. **Scoop app-dir named `cli`** — the release pipeline now sets the Scoop manifest name to `entire`, so it installs under `…\scoop\apps\entire\` instead of `…\apps\cli\`.

- `ENTIRE_BIN` was never honored outside the test harness, so that workaround was a no-op — the symlink fallback removes the need for it.
- **Existing Scoop users on `cli` won't auto-migrate**: run `scoop uninstall cli && scoop install entire` once the next release lands.
- Windows **Authenticode signing** / Smart App Control (mentioned as possibly-related) is tracked separately in #1505.

The fix will be in the next release. If you can retest on Windows 11 + Cursor + Scoop once it ships, a confirmation here would be appreciated.

{"body":"[https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/841](<https://entire.io/gh/entireio/cli/trails/841>)

Fixes entireio/cli#1424.

## Background

entireio/cli#1424 reports that on Windows 11 (Scoop install, Cursor), Entire records nothing — `session list` / `checkpoint list` stay at 0 even though `entire status` shows enabled and hooks look correctly configured. Investigation found **three independent root causes** stacked together.

## Root causes & fixes

### 1\. Scoop installs the app dir as `cli`, not `entire`

The published bucket manifest is literally `cli.json` (verified live), so the binary lands at `…\scoop\apps\cli\current\entire.exe`. GoReleaser defaults the scoop manifest name to the project name, which resolves to the repo name (`cli`). The `scoops:` block set no `name:`.

**Fix:** set `scoops[].name: entire`.

### 2\. `--absolute-git-hook-path` fails on Scoop's `current\` junction

`hookCmdPrefix` calls `filepath.EvalSymlinks(os.Executable())`, which can't resolve Scoop's `current\` **NTFS directory junction** and returns *"The system cannot find the path specified."* — the exact error in the report. This blocks `entire enable --agent cursor`, `agent add cursor`, and `configure --absolute-git-hook-path`.

**Fix:** on Windows, fall back to the unresolved `os.Executable()` path (extracted into `resolveHookExePath` so all branches are unit-tested cross-platform). That path is valid and, on Scoop, actually **more stable** than the resolved one — `current\` survives version updates that repoint the junction, whereas a resolved versioned path disappears on the next update.

### 3\. Cursor agent hooks silently never fire on Windows (the actual "nothing recorded")

`cursor.InstallHooks` hardcoded the POSIX `sh -c '…'` wrapper. Cursor spawns hook commands via the native OS shell, so on a Windows host with no runnable POSIX `sh` the wrapper fails to launch — and because it's the *silent* wrapper, the failure is swallowed (no hook, no error). The shared OS-aware path (`UseWindowsProductionHooks` + `WrapProductionSilentHookCommandForOS`) already exists and was built explicitly "so the other sh-based agents can adopt the Windows fallback" (commit `1cf8eadc2`) — but only codex had adopted it.

**Fix:** migrate Cursor to the shared path. It's **probe-gated**: a no-op on non-Windows and on Windows hosts where `sh` works; it only swaps in the native `cmd.exe` wrapper when no `sh` is present.

## Scope notes

* The other sh-based agents (gemini, claude-code, factory-droid) still hardcode the sh wrapper and have the same latent bug; **copilot-cli deliberately stays sh-based** because it runs hook commands via a `bash` field (not the native shell), so the cmd.exe wrapper would break it. A blanket migration is unsafe — auditing each agent's execution model is left to a follow-up.
* Windows **Authenticode signing** (Smart App Control) is a separate issue (entireio/cli#1505), not addressed here.
* Existing Scoop users on `cli` won't auto-migrate; they'd `scoop uninstall cli` + `scoop install entire`. The stale `cli.json` in the bucket can be removed separately.

## Tests

* `resolveHookExePath`: resolves normally / Windows falls back on failure / non-Windows surfaces the error (injected GOOS + resolver, runs on any host).
* Cursor: Windows probe-success keeps sh wrappers; probe-failure installs cmd.exe wrappers (via `SetWindowsHookProbeForTesting`).
* `go build ./...`, `golangci-lint` (changed pkgs), and `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/agent/... ./cmd/entire/cli/strategy/...` all pass locally.

{"body":"`factoryai-droid` recorded no checkpoints on Windows. Commits landed normally and not one agent hook fired, so no session ever existed for the commit hook to condense. It passed on Linux and macOS throughout.

## Cause

Entire writes droid's hook command as:

```
sh -c 'if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks factoryai-droid session-start'
```

Droid's **Windows** build hands every hook command to `cmd.exe`; only its macOS/Linux build uses `sh`. cmd.exe reads that string's `>` as its own redirection and `&` as a command separator, so the line is cut apart and `entire` is never executed — with **exit code 0**, which is why nothing reported a problem.

Read out of the shipped droid binaries, and consistent across every version checked:

| droid build | how it runs a hook command |
| --- | --- |
| darwin 0.215.1 | `{command, shell: "sh"}` |
| windows 0.109.1 | `spawn("cmd.exe", ["/c", H])` |
| windows 0.178.0 | `{command, shell: "cmd.exe"}` |
| windows 0.215.1 | `spawn(%ComSpec%, ["/d","/s","/c",H], {windowsVerbatimArguments:true})` |

## Fix

Droid installs the native cmd.exe wrappers whenever the host is Windows, via a new `agent.HookHostIsWindows()`.

Deliberately **not** gated on the existing `agent.UseWindowsProductionHooks`. That probe only establishes that `sh -c 'exit 0'` runs — a command carrying no cmd.exe metacharacters — so a Windows host with Git Bash reports success and keeps the broken wrapper. This is not hypothetical: both the machine used for verification and the GitHub Windows runner have `sh` on PATH, so the probe would have succeeded on each. Codex and Cursor keep the probe, but not because their runners differ — this repo describes those as going through cmd.exe too. Codex keeps it on evidence: it demonstrably passes the Windows nightly with the sh wrapper installed, so whatever its composition does, the wrapper survives it. Cursor has no such evidence, and may share this defect; see Not covered.

Also adds `WrapProductionPlainTextWarningHookCommandForOS`, the missing selector for the one wrapper shape droid uses that had no `ForOS` variant.

Migration needed no new code: `dropStaleEntireHooks` already replaces a managed hook that is not the wanted one, and `IsManagedHookCommand` recognises both Windows shapes. There is a test pinning that, since it is what stops a repo carrying both entries and double-firing.

## Verification

Run [34462110574](https://github.com/entireio/cli/actions/runs/34462110574) — the previously failing test, on a real Windows runner, against real droid, built from this branch's code (`0.0.0-20260910094138-bb2b7c9257cf`): `Total: 1  Passed: 1  Failed: 0`.

That run needed a throwaway change to `e2e-windows.yml`, which is hardcoded to claude-code. **That change is deliberately not part of this PR**, so the run is evidence but is not reproducible from this branch as it stands — there is no source-built Windows workflow here that can target droid.

Artifact, against the original failure:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| agent hooks in `entire.log` | none | session-start, user-prompt-submit, stop, session-end (×2 each) |
| `prepare-commit-msg` | "no active sessions" | "agent commit trailer added" |
| checkpoint trailers | 0 | 2 |

Additionally, on a separate Windows ARM64 machine: the old wrapper pasted at a cmd prompt exits 0 and never creates `.entire\logs` at all, while the new one reaches hook dispatch and logs a real lifecycle event; and both of droid's shell compositions (0.178.0's and 0.215.1's) were exercised through a byte-exact model of `windowsVerbatimArguments`, since droid nests our stored string inside its own `cmd.exe /d /s /c`.

## The other two commits

- **`key the install-test expectations to the host`** — three existing droid tests hardcoded the sh wrapper, so on a Windows host they asserted a command `InstallHooks` no longer writes. CI would not have caught it: the Windows job runs `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'` and none of those names match. Confirmed by same-commit before/after on a Windows box: 13 assertion failures → 0.
- **`nightly-e2e: put factoryai-droid back on the Windows agent list`** — restores the three things the exclusion comment named. Note this workflow installs the *published nightly* and checks out the tag it resolves, so it does not test this branch; droid there is first exercised on the scheduled run after a nightly carrying this fix ships. A dispatch before then would install a pre-fix nightly and fail misleadingly.

## Existing Windows installs need a re-enable

There is no drift signal for this. Droid implements no `HookFreshness` (claude-code, codex, opencode and pi do), so `status` and `doctor` will not report the stale sh wrapper, and `AreHooksInstalled` still answers true for it. A repo already enabled on Windows keeps its broken hooks until someone re-runs `entire enable`, which is what performs the migration. Giving droid a `HookFreshness` is the durable fix and is not in this PR.

## Version scope

Verified end to end on droid 0.178.0 and 0.215.1. 0.109.1 spawned `cmd.exe /c <H>` *without* `windowsVerbatimArguments`, so libuv backslash-escapes the inner quotes of the nested silent wrapper into something cmd.exe does not parse. That version stays broken — equally broken as before, since the sh wrapper never survived its cmd.exe either. Switching every hook to the bare wrapper shape would likely fix it; not taken here because it would trade the shape verified on current droid for one that is not.

## Not covered

The subagent path (`PreToolUse`/`PostToolUse[Task]`) is not exercised by this test.

No Windows workflow in the repo builds from source and can target an agent other than claude-code, so a future Windows-specific agent fix has no pre-merge check either — the nightly smoke can only test what has already shipped.

Cursor may share this defect. Its `InstallHooks` comment says it too spawns hooks through cmd.exe on Windows, in which case its `UseWindowsProductionHooks` probe is wrong for the same reason droid's was — but it is excluded from the Windows matrix (no tmux), so there is no evidence either way. Settling that means reading its runner the way droid's was read; deliberately out of scope here.

input.summary: Ask Windows box to read Cursor's hook runner
input.message:
Need you to read Cursor IDE's hook-command runner out of the SHIPPED Windows build, and (secondary) run two candidate wrappers through its exact composition. Context: I'm establishing whether Entire's `sh -c '…'` hook wrapper survives Cursor on Windows. I read the macOS build (Cursor 3.19.13) and found PowerShell, not cmd.exe — I need the Windows build to confirm, because I must not infer Windows behaviour from a mac bundle.

## Task A — read the file (this is the deliverable I need most)

Find Cursor's install. Typical paths:
- `%LOCALAPPDATA%\Programs\cursor\resources\app\out\vs\workbench\api\node\extensionHostProcess.js`
- or `C:\Program Files\cursor\resources\app\out\…` (system install)

If Cursor is not installed, download and install it silently — it's an Inno Setup 6.4 installer (my local innoextract 1.9 can't parse it, which is why I'm asking you):
```
curl.exe -L -o "$env:TEMP\CursorUserSetup-x64-3.19.19.exe" "https://downloads.cursor.com/production/6496ea8a068aebfcd21990e70ff522e9abf10c8c/win32/x64/user-setup/CursorUserSetup-x64-3.19.19.exe"
# Inno silent, no need to launch the app:
& "$env:TEMP\CursorUserSetup-x64-3.19.19.exe" /VERYSILENT /SUPPRESSMSGBOXES /NORESTART /NOICONS
```
(ARM64 box — if x64 won't install, use `.../win32/arm64/user-setup/CursorUserSetup-arm64-3.19.19.exe`.) Say which build and version you actually read.

Then, from `extensionHostProcess.js` (one huge line — use offsets, not line numbers), print the surrounding ~1200 chars for each of these, verbatim:

1. `$executeHookDirect` — the method body.
2. The array literal `["-NoProfile","-NonInteractive","-ExecutionPolicy","Bypass"]` — does it exist, and is it the `shellArgs` that `$executeHookDirect` passes?
3. `Get-Content -LiteralPath` — the payload-transport composition (I expect a function taking (payloadPath, command)).
4. `function` … `process.platform!=="win32"` … `pwsh` … `WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe` — the shell resolver.
5. `NaiveTerminalExecutor.execute` — the actual `spawn(...)`, specifically whether the shell/args come from `options.shell` / `options.shellArgs` or fall through to `"/bin/sh"`.
6. Grep the whole file for `cmd.exe` and print each hit's context — I want to know whether ANY hook path goes through cmd.exe.

What I read in the mac build, for you to confirm or contradict (please contradict loudly if it differs):
- hook spawn is `spawn(<powershell>, ["-NoProfile","-NonInteractive","-ExecutionPolicy","Bypass","-c", SCRIPT], {env, cwd, stdio:["ignore","pipe","pipe"]})`
- `<powershell>` = `pwsh` if on PATH, else `powershell`, else `%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`; throws if none
- `SCRIPT` = `$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Content -LiteralPath '<tmp>\cursor-hook-payload-<pid>-<ts>-<rand>.json' -Raw | & { $input | <HOOK_COMMAND> }`
- `<HOOK_COMMAND>` is the `command` string from `.cursor/hooks.json` inserted verbatim, with a `& ` prefix added only when it starts with `'` or `"`
- on Windows the JSON payload goes via that temp file; on non-Windows it goes via stdin and the shell is `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh`

## Task B — does it survive? (secondary, but very useful)

Model the composition byte-exactly and see which wrappers reach their target. Save as `probe.ps1` and run it, then paste the whole output plus the contents of `$env:TEMP\hookprobe\`:

```powershell
$ErrorActionPreference = 'Continue'
$d = "$env:TEMP\hookprobe"; Remove-Item -Recurse -Force $d -EA SilentlyContinue; New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force $d | Out-Null

# stub that stands in for `entire`: records its argv and its stdin
@'
@echo off
echo ARGS: %* >> "%TEMP%\hookprobe\stub.log"
more >> "%TEMP%\hookprobe\stub-stdin.log"
exit /b 0
'@ | Set-Content -Encoding ASCII "$d\entire.cmd"
$env:PATH = "$d;$env:PATH"

'{"hook_event_name":"stop","conversation_id":"abc"}' | Set-Content -NoNewline -Encoding UTF8 "$d\payload.json"

$ps = (Get-Command pwsh -EA SilentlyContinue)?.Source
if (-not $ps) { $ps = (Get-Command powershell).Source }
"powershell used: $ps"
"sh on PATH: " + [bool](Get-Command sh -EA SilentlyContinue) + " -> " + (Get-Command sh -EA SilentlyContinue)?.Source

$wrappers = @{
  'sh'  = "sh -c 'if ! command -v entire >/dev/null 2>&1; then exit 0; fi; exec entire hooks cursor stop'"
  'cmd' = 'cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire >nul 2>nul & if errorlevel 1 (ver>nul) else (entire hooks cursor stop)"'
  'bare'= 'entire hooks cursor stop'
}
foreach ($k in 'sh','cmd','bare') {
  $H = $wrappers[$k]
  "`n===== $k =====`nHOOK_COMMAND: $H"
  Remove-Item "$d\stub.log","$d\stub-stdin.log" -EA SilentlyContinue
  $script = "`$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Content -LiteralPath '$d\payload.json' -Raw | & { `$input | $H }"
  "SCRIPT: $script"
  & $ps -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c $script 2>&1 | ForEach-Object { "  out: $_" }
  "exit: $LASTEXITCODE"
  "stub.log:       " + ((Get-Content "$d\stub.log" -EA SilentlyContinue) -join ' | ')
  "stub-stdin.log: " + ((Get-Content "$d\stub-stdin.log" -EA SilentlyContinue) -join ' | ')
}
```
What I'm looking for per wrapper: did the stub run at all (stub.log non-empty), did it get the right argv (`hooks cursor stop`), and did the JSON payload reach its stdin. Then repeat the `sh` case with `sh` removed from PATH (`$env:PATH` filtered, or rename the Git `sh.exe` for one run) so I can see the no-sh failure mode and its exit code.

Report back with the raw snippets — don't summarise the code, I need the actual text. If any of this is blocked by your permissions, say so rather than working around it.

input.summary: Addendum: the PATH-divergence test is now the crux
input.message:
Addendum to my previous request — one small test has become the crux, please do it even if the rest is still in progress. I now think Entire's Windows Cursor bug is a PATH divergence, not a shell-quoting problem, and it's decided by whether `sh` resolves in PowerShell.

Mechanism I want to confirm or kill: Entire decides which hook wrapper to write by running `sh -c 'exit 0'` in the `entire enable` process. Cursor then runs the hook through PowerShell (`powershell -c "... | & { $input | <HOOK_COMMAND> }"`), which has a different PATH. Git for Windows' default install puts `sh.exe` in `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` (and `Git\bin`), neither of which is on the machine PATH — only `Git\cmd` is. So `entire enable` run from Git Bash sees `sh`, writes the `sh -c '…'` wrapper, and Cursor's PowerShell then cannot resolve `sh`. Issue #1424's reporter was on exactly that setup (Windows 11 + Git Bash MINGW64).

Please run and paste raw output:

1. In **PowerShell**:
```powershell
$env:PATH -split ';'
Get-Command sh -EA SilentlyContinue | Format-List Name,Source
Get-Command bash -EA SilentlyContinue | Format-List Name,Source
Get-Command git -EA SilentlyContinue | Format-List Name,Source
Get-ChildItem 'C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\sh.exe','C:\Program Files\Git\bin\sh.exe' -EA SilentlyContinue | Select FullName
& powershell -NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c "sh -c 'exit 0'; 'exit=' + $LASTEXITCODE"
```
2. In **Git Bash** (if installed):
```bash
command -v sh; echo "PATH=$PATH"
```

What I'm after: does `sh` resolve in PowerShell's PATH, does it resolve in Git Bash's, and is `sh.exe` present on disk but off the machine PATH. If `sh` resolves in PowerShell on your box too, say so plainly — that weakens my mechanism and I'd rather know now than after I've written a PR around it.

Also, if it's cheap: the exit code and stderr of the PowerShell one-liner above when `sh` is NOT resolvable — I want to know what Cursor would see (I expect a non-zero exit and a `The term 'sh' is not recognized` on stderr, which Cursor swallows).

input.summary: Runner evidence: Cursor uses PowerShell, not cmd.exe
input.message:
Runner read out of the shipped binaries: **Cursor does not use cmd.exe for hooks — it uses PowerShell.** The defect is real, but the mechanism in `cursor/hooks.go:124-132` is wrong, and so is the reason the probe fails. Nothing edited yet.

## What Cursor actually does on Windows

Both Windows runners compose the same thing. Spawn:

```
spawn(<powershell>, ["-NoProfile","-NonInteractive","-ExecutionPolicy","Bypass","-c", SCRIPT],
      {env, cwd, stdio:["ignore","pipe","pipe"]})     // IDE; CLI omits the four flags
```
```
SCRIPT = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Content -LiteralPath '<tmp>\cursor-hook-payload-<pid>-<ts>-<rand>.json' -Raw | & { $input | <HOOK_COMMAND> }
```

`<powershell>` = `pwsh` if on PATH, else `powershell`, else `%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe`; it *throws* if none. `<HOOK_COMMAND>` is our `.cursor/hooks.json` `command` string inserted verbatim, with a `& ` prefix added only if it starts with `'` or `"`. The JSON payload goes via that temp file on Windows and via stdin on macOS/Linux (where the shell is `$SHELL` else `/bin/sh`, `-c`). Sandbox policy is `insecure_none` for hooks, so it is a plain `spawn`, no sandbox helper in the path.

Grepped the whole extension-host bundle for `cmd.exe`: seven hits, none on a hook path (comspec default, debug-terminal defaults, shell-type detection for the debug terminal, the `.bat`/`.ps1` *file* launcher, and the sandbox spawn branch that hooks never reach).

Evidence, and it is per-platform where the brief said it had to be:

| build read | how it runs a hook command |
| --- | --- |
| cursor-agent CLI, **windows/x64** `agent-cli-package.zip` 2026.09.08-6caf4ff | powershell `-c`, temp-file payload, `Get-Content … \| & { $input \| H }` |
| cursor-agent CLI, darwin/arm64, same version | `$SHELL`/`/bin/sh -c`, stdin payload, POSIX heredoc |
| Cursor IDE 3.19.13, 3.15.19, 3.11.19 (extension host) | powershell `-NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -c`, temp-file payload, identical `Get-Content` string |

The CLI's mac and Windows bundles differ in exactly the folded spots — `getCommandHookPayloadTransportMode()` returns `"stdin"` on mac and `"windows_temp_file"` on Windows for the same option value, and the here-doc/here-string flag flips from `!1` to `!0` — so reading the mac build alone would have been wrong about the Windows path. The IDE bundle is *not* folded (its `_getBackendOS()===1` branch is present in the mac build; `1` is Windows, confirmed against `i===1?"Windows":i===2?"Macintosh":"Linux"`), and the composed string is byte-identical across all four builds above, only minifier identifiers differing. windows-mate is confirming the Windows IDE build directly; I will not write the doc comment until that lands.

Version stability: identical at 3.11.19 (2026-07-13 — the day #1424 was closed), 3.15.19, 3.19.13. So Cursor was already PowerShell when #1735 shipped on the cmd.exe premise. Nothing like droid's three compositions.

## Which runner matters on Windows: both

There **is** a native Windows cursor-agent CLI — docs' "Windows (native)" is `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex`, and the package is `https://downloads.cursor.com/lab/<ver>/windows/<arch>/agent-cli-package.**zip**`. (A `.tar.gz` probe on that path 403s, which is what first made me think there was no Windows CLI — worth knowing if anyone re-checks.) It installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-agent\versions\`. Both it and the IDE read the project's `.cursor/hooks.json`, so the one file has to work under both — and it does, because they compose the same thing.

## The real mechanism: PATH divergence, not quote mangling

The `sh -c '…'` wrapper survives PowerShell fine. PowerShell single quotes are literal, so `>`, `2>&1` and `;` inside them never reach the parser, and the whole script is handed to `sh` as one argv element. Nothing is cut apart the way cmd.exe would cut it. So the brief's predicted failure does not happen.

What fails is *resolving `sh` at all*, and the probe asks the wrong process:

- `UseWindowsProductionHooks` runs `cmd.exe /d /s /c "sh -c 'exit 0'"` with the **`entire enable` process's** environment.
- Cursor runs the hook in a **PowerShell it spawns**, with the machine/user PATH.
- Git for Windows' default install puts `sh.exe` in `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` and `…\Git\bin`. Neither is on the machine PATH — only `…\Git\cmd` is. And MSYS translates PATH for native children, so a probe launched from Git Bash sees `sh` while Cursor's PowerShell does not.

So `entire enable` run from Git Bash succeeds the probe, writes the sh wrapper, and Cursor then cannot run it. That is exactly #1424's environment — Windows 11 + Git Bash (MINGW64) — which is why the retest confirmation the close comment asked for never arrived: under the shipped fix that user is still broken. The probe is not merely too weak, as it was for droid; for Cursor it is measuring a different process's PATH, which no amount of strengthening the probe command fixes.

That lands on the same change you specified — gate on host-is-Windows — but the doc comment has to say this, not cmd.exe. I'd also drop the "silent wrapper swallows the failure" line: here PowerShell writes `The term 'sh' is not recognized` to stderr and exits non-zero, and it is *Cursor* that discards it (`this.logger.logError` into its own log, `{}` returned to the caller).

## Still open before I touch code

1. windows-mate confirming the Windows IDE build, and confirming `sh` does not resolve in PowerShell while it does in Git Bash on a real box. If `sh` resolves in PowerShell there, my mechanism weakens and I'll say so rather than build on it.
2. Whether our cmd.exe wrapper actually survives being nested in that PowerShell pipeline **and still receives the JSON payload on stdin**. On paper it does — PowerShell passes the double-quoted string as one argv element, `cmd /s` strips exactly the outer pair, and stdin inherits through cmd to `entire` — but "on paper" is how #1735 got here, so it is being run for real, with a stub standing in for `entire` that records its argv and its stdin. If the payload does *not* survive the nesting, the answer is not the cmd wrapper and I'll come back before writing anything.
3. `agent.HookHostIsWindows()` doesn't exist on `main`; it's on #2349. I'll either stack on that branch or add the helper, whichever you prefer — say if you have a preference.

## One more finding, cursor-side and not fixable by us

The Windows **CLI** picks its shell executor by *terminal type*: `Ut()` returns a **bash** executor whenever `MSYSTEM` is set (i.e. run from Git Bash) or Git-for-Windows bash is found, *before* it ever considers PowerShell — while the hook script is still composed as PowerShell, because that branch is chosen by build platform. So `cursor-agent` started from Git Bash on Windows feeds `$OutputEncoding = […]; Get-Content … | & { … }` to `bash -c`, which cannot parse it. Hooks are dead there whatever we install. Belongs in the PR as a caveat on the fix's reach, not as something we work around.

Will report back with the verification results before opening anything.

content.text:
Evidence gathered and reported to the peer session. Here's where it stands:

**The suspicion was right that Cursor's Windows hooks are broken, but wrong about why — Cursor uses PowerShell, not cmd.exe.**

Read out of the shipped binaries (Windows `agent-cli-package.zip` for the CLI, plus Cursor IDE 3.11.19/3.15.19/3.19.13 extension hosts):

```
spawn(<powershell>, ["-NoProfile","-NonInteractive","-ExecutionPolicy","Bypass","-c", SCRIPT])
SCRIPT = $OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Content -LiteralPath '<tmp>\cursor-hook-payload-…json' -Raw | & { $input | <HOOK_COMMAND> }
```

Zero `cmd.exe` on any hook path. The composition is byte-identical across all four builds read, including 3.11.19 — released the day #1424 was closed — so the shipped #1735 fix was written on a false premise.

The reading was worth doing per-platform: the CLI's mac and Windows bundles differ in exactly the folded spots (transport mode returns `"stdin"` vs `"windows_temp_file"`, here-doc vs here-string), so the mac build alone would have misled. There *is* a native Windows cursor-agent CLI (`irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex`, a `.zip` not a `.tar.gz`), so both runners exist on Windows and both compose the same thing.

The real defect: `sh -c '…'` survives PowerShell quoting fine — single quotes are literal, nothing gets cut apart. It fails because `sh` has to resolve in *Cursor's* PowerShell PATH, while `UseWindowsProductionHooks` probes it in the `entire enable` process's PATH. Git for Windows puts `sh.exe` in `Git\usr\bin`/`Git\bin`, neither on the machine PATH, and MSYS translates PATH for native children — so `entire enable` from Git Bash passes the probe and writes a wrapper Cursor cannot run. That is exactly #1424's environment, and no strengthening of the probe command fixes it, because it is measuring the wrong process.

Same conclusion as the brief (gate on host-is-Windows), different reason for the doc comment.

Two things pending with `windows-mate` before I touch code: confirming the Windows IDE build directly, and confirming our cmd.exe wrapper both survives nesting in that PowerShell pipeline *and* still receives the JSON payload on stdin — if the payload doesn't survive, the cmd wrapper isn't the answer and the fix changes shape.

One extra finding for the PR: the Windows CLI picks a **bash** executor whenever `MSYSTEM` is set, while still composing the script as PowerShell — so `cursor-agent` launched from Git Bash has dead hooks whatever we install. Cursor-side, not ours.

Another Claude session sent a message:
<cross-session-message from="uds:/tmp/cc-socks/6563.sock" from-name="uninstall-ext-6b" from-mode="prompting">
Evidence accepted — my brief's mechanism was wrong and yours supersedes it. cmd.exe quote mangling was the droid mechanism and I carried it over as a prediction; PowerShell single quotes are literal, so the sh wrapper does survive the parse and the failure is `sh` not resolving. Drop the "silent wrapper swallows it" line too, as you say: PowerShell reports the error and Cursor discards it, which is a different sentence with a different owner.

**Stack on #2349.** Branch off `fix-droid-ai-windows-test` and say so in the PR body. Two agents adding `HookHostIsWindows` to the same package independently is a duplicate declaration the moment both merge, and this is the repo's normal shape for dependent work (the Windows installer work stacked the same way). #2349 is code-complete and green except an approval and the CodeQL default-setup conflict, neither of which you can unblock; if it stalls, rebase onto main after it merges rather than duplicating the helper.

Since you will be editing `hook_command.go` anyway: **`HookHostIsWindows`'s doc needs generalizing in your PR.** #2349 wrote it around droid's cmd.exe metacharacters and left "Cursor has no such evidence, and may share this defect; see Not covered." You now have that evidence, and it is a second mechanism for the same predicate — the agent runs the hook in a process whose environment we cannot vouch for, so a probe run from *our* process answers a question about the wrong PATH. That is a stronger and more general justification for the gate than the quote-mangling one; say both mechanisms and stop implying the answer is unknown.

## Two things to add to your open item 2

Your stub test is the right instrument. Two specifics that would otherwise bite after merge:

**The payload encoding, and `powershell.exe` 5.1 specifically.** `$OutputEncoding` in Windows PowerShell 5.1 defaults to ASCII, which is *why* Cursor sets it — and `[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` in 5.1 is the BOM-carrying encoder. So `$input | <native.exe>` there can prepend a UTF-8 BOM to the JSON your hook reads on stdin, and #1424's reporter mentioning "correct UTF-8 encoding (no BOM)" is a hint this has bitten someone already. Test whether `entire hooks cursor <verb>` tolerates a leading BOM on stdin, and test it under **both** shells, because the resolution chain prefers `pwsh` and falls back to `powershell`, so both branches ship. Our known Windows box is PowerShell-5.1-only, which makes it the right box for that branch and means pwsh needs covering separately.

**What the fix actually moves the dependency to.** The cmd.exe wrapper opens with `where.exe entire`, and if `entire` is not on the PATH *Cursor's child* sees, that wrapper exits 0 silently — the same class of failure, one binary over. So the fix does not remove the PATH dependency, it moves it from "`sh` on the child's PATH", which Git for Windows' default install does not satisfy (only `…\Git\cmd` is on the machine PATH), to "`entire` on the child's PATH", which every documented install method does satisfy. Worth stating exactly that way in the PR, and worth having the stub confirm the absent-`entire` branch too, so the claim is measured rather than argued. If it turns out `entire` is not reliably visible there either, the answer is an absolute path in the hook command, not a wrapper swap — come back before writing that.

## On the bash-executor finding

Good find, and it belongs in the PR as a caveat — but scope it precisely so it does not read as "the fix does not work": it is the **CLI** started from Git Bash, chosen by `MSYSTEM`, while #1424 was the **IDE**, which is unaffected. So the fix does help the original reporter; what it cannot help is `cursor-agent` launched from Git Bash on Windows, where hooks are dead whatever we install. Two sentences, with the reason it is cursor's to fix.

Hold off on the doc comment until windows-mate lands, as you planned. If `sh` does resolve in Cursor's PowerShell on a real box, report that before adjusting the mechanism — a weakened mechanism is still worth writing down, and the gate change may survive on the general argument alone.

input.message:
Second addendum — please capture the hook's stdin as RAW BYTES, not lines. I've just confirmed locally that a leading UTF-8 BOM makes Entire's hook input parse fail outright, so whether PowerShell prepends one is now as important as whether the wrapper runs at all.

Why: Entire decodes hook input with Go's `json.NewDecoder(...).Decode(...)`, which does not skip a BOM. Measured here:
```
plain  err=<nil>                                                            raw={"conversation_id":"abc"}
bom    err=invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value              raw=
```
Cursor sets `$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` before piping the payload, and in **Windows PowerShell 5.1** that encoder is the BOM-carrying one. If PowerShell emits the preamble when writing to a native command's stdin, every Cursor hook on a 5.1 box fails to parse regardless of which wrapper we install — and #1424's reporter volunteering that their `hooks.json` had "correct UTF-8 encoding (no BOM)" suggests someone has already been bitten by something in this area. Your box being 5.1-only makes it exactly the right one to answer this.

So replace the `more >>` stub from my first message with a byte-capturing one. Two files:

`%TEMP%\hookprobe\capture.ps1`:
```powershell
$in = [Console]::OpenStandardInput()
$ms = New-Object System.IO.MemoryStream
$in.CopyTo($ms)
[IO.File]::WriteAllBytes("$env:TEMP\hookprobe\stdin.bin", $ms.ToArray())
```

`%TEMP%\hookprobe\entire.cmd` (the stub that stands in for the real binary, first on PATH):
```
@echo off
echo ARGS: %* >> "%TEMP%\hookprobe\stub.log"
powershell -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File "%TEMP%\hookprobe\capture.ps1"
exit /b 0
```

Then, per wrapper case, after running the composition, paste:
```powershell
Get-Content "$env:TEMP\hookprobe\stub.log"
$b = [IO.File]::ReadAllBytes("$env:TEMP\hookprobe\stdin.bin")
"len=$($b.Length)"
"first16=" + (($b[0..15] | ForEach-Object { $_.ToString('x2') }) -join ' ')
[Text.Encoding]::UTF8.GetString($b)
```
`ef bb bf` at the front is the BOM and is the answer I'm looking for. Run it under **`powershell`** (5.1) and, if `pwsh` is installed, under **`pwsh`** too — Cursor's resolution chain prefers `pwsh` and falls back to `powershell`, so both branches ship and they may differ here. input.summary: Drop Task A; one isolated repro needed for the cmd guard
input.message:
Excellent work, and thank you for catching your own harness error before it reached me — "the cmd wrapper cannot survive PowerShell" is exactly the PR I would have written on it. Three things.

**Drop Task A entirely.** Your permission classifier denied the download; that's your boundary and I'm not asking you to revisit it or ask your user for it. I'm extracting the shipped Windows installer on my own machine instead (Inno Setup 6.4, so it needed a newer innoextract than the released one — that's building now). Please don't spend anything more on it.

**Also don't install pwsh.** Same reason. I'd rather ship with the pwsh branch explicitly marked uncovered than have you request an install for my benefit. For the record, my expectation — unverified, and it will be labelled as such — is that PowerShell 7 does *not* write the preamble to a native command's stdin, so the BOM is a 5.1-specific defect; the fix tolerates a BOM either way, so it doesn't hinge on that.

**One isolated repro, please, because your case 5 conflicts with our CI.** This repo has a Windows-only test that runs the very same wrapper on a real Windows runner with `entire` absent, and asserts the wrapped command does **not** run — it wraps `echo <marker>` and fails if the marker reaches stdout. It passes on every CI run. Your case 5 says the else branch was taken, which would print the marker and fail that test. One of the two observations has a hidden variable in it, and since it decides whether a wrapper we already ship to codex and droid has a broken guard, I'd like to know which.

Cheapest isolation — no PowerShell in the picture at all, and print the intermediate errorlevel:

```
cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire & echo EL=%errorlevel%"
cmd.exe /d /s /c "where.exe entire >nul 2>nul & if errorlevel 1 (echo GUARD_HELD) else (echo GUARD_MISFIRED)"
```
run once with `entire` reachable and once with it not, and please paste the exact `PATH` each run saw (`cmd.exe /d /s /c "echo %PATH%"` under the same env you used for case 5).

The specific hypothesis I'd like ruled out: your case-5 run went through node's `spawnSync` with a custom `env`, and on Windows it is easy to end up with **both `Path` and `PATH`** in the child environment, after which different consumers can resolve against different values — which would let `where.exe` succeed while cmd's own command lookup fails, and that is precisely the shape of what you saw (`errorlevel` 0 → else branch → `'entire' is not recognized` from cmd, not from where). If that's it, the guard is fine and your harness had one more wrinkle. If the two cmd-only lines above print GUARD_MISFIRED with a clean single-cased PATH, the guard is genuinely broken and that becomes its own issue affecting codex and droid too — worth knowing either way, and no rush.

For the record, the things you established that I'm now building on: the BOM is real and is Cursor's own `$OutputEncoding` line, one per codepage-independent producer with a second from cp65001; the real `entire.exe` failed end-to-end with the exact error I'd measured synthetically; every failure path exits 0, so Cursor sees success and there is nothing for it to swallow; and the stock Git for Windows layout has both `sh.exe` copies off the machine PATH. I'm citing your box as the witness for the BOM and for the Git layout, and explicitly *not* as a witness for the PATH mechanism, since scoop's shim rescues `sh` there — your call to flag that yourself is the reason the PR won't overclaim.

input.summary: BOM confirmed end-to-end; parser fix written and green
input.message:
Capture landed: the BOM is real, confirmed by the shipped binary, not a stub. Parser fix is written, lint-clean, and green across every agent package. Three corrections from the measurement change what we write.

**The confirmation is stronger than a stub run.** On windows-mate's first attempt, before anything was stubbed, the sh wrapper resolved the real `entire.exe` on PATH and it printed:

```
failed to parse hook event: failed to parse hook input: invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value
```

Isolated by varying console codepage against the presence of Cursor's own `$OutputEncoding` line, 50-byte payload:

```
cp1252   line=True  -> len=55  ef bb bf 7b 22 ...
cp1252   line=False -> len=52  7b 22 ...
cp65001  line=True  -> len=58  ef bb bf ef bb bf 7b 22 ...
cp65001  line=False -> len=55  ef bb bf 7b 22 ...
```

So Cursor's line adds one BOM at any codepage under 5.1 (the default `$OutputEncoding` there is ASCII, which is *why* Cursor sets it), and a UTF-8 console codepage adds a second independently. **They stack** — which is the one place I departed from your spec: `skipUTF8BOM` loops rather than stripping once, because a cp65001 box measurably sends two. It terminates when the input does, and the plugin boundary bounds the input with the existing ceiling. All three of your details are in: reader errors not propagated (so `"empty hook input"` is untouched — it is asserted in five files, not just `event_test.go`), `StdinLooksInteractive` still on the raw `stdin` ahead of the wrapping, and the skipper named and separately documented.

Also measured, and needing no code: PowerShell appends a trailing CRLF, which the streaming decoder already ignores.

The gate is pinned rather than asserted. I extended `TestReadHookInputRawLimited_ReturnsBeforeEOF` into two cases instead of writing a second near-identical test — the new case is a `{}` payload with the pipe held open, shorter than a BOM. Ungating the peek makes exactly that case fail:

```
--- FAIL: TestReadHookInputRawLimited_ReturnsBeforeEOF/shorter_than_a_BOM (3.00s)
        ReadHookInputRawLimited blocked waiting for EOF — regression of #1398
```

The existing 26-byte case does not catch it, so without that case the gate would have been comment-only.

## Three corrections for the wrapper PR

1. **Every failure path exits 0, including the missing-`sh` one.** I had us saying PowerShell reports the error and Cursor discards it. Half wrong: a `CommandNotFoundException` raised inside `& { $input | … }` does not set `powershell.exe`'s exit code, so Cursor sees a clean success. Standalone the same command exits 1; inside the hook pipeline it is 0. The failure is invisible at the exit-code level, not merely ignored — a stronger and simpler sentence than the one we had.

2. **The cmd wrapper does survive the PowerShell nesting**, with correct argv and the payload delivered. Their first harness used `Start-Process -ArgumentList`, which mangles inner double quotes and produced a bogus `AmpersandNotAllowed`; re-run through node's `spawnSync` with an args array — Cursor's actual mechanism — it works. They caught that themselves before it reached me.

3. **The PATH mechanism is intact but their box is not a clean witness, and I won't cite it as one.** `sh` *does* resolve in PowerShell there — because scoop's shims directory is on the machine PATH and provides `sh.exe`. What they did confirm directly is the stock layout: `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\sh.exe` and `…\Git\bin\sh.exe` both exist, neither directory is on the machine PATH, only `…\Git\cmd` is. So the PR cites the on-disk layout plus case 2 (sh absent → wrapper runs, stub never invoked, exit 0), not "measured on a box where it happened".

## Two open, neither blocking the parser PR

**Their case 5 says our cmd guard misfires**, and I'm not accepting it yet: `where.exe entire >nul 2>nul & if errorlevel 1 (ver>nul) else (…)` took the else branch with `entire` absent and printed `'entire' is not recognized`. That contradicts `TestWindowsWrappers_Execution`, which runs the same wrapper on a real Windows runner with `entire` absent, wraps `echo <marker>`, and fails if the marker reaches stdout — and passes every run. I've asked for a cmd-only repro with the intermediate errorlevel and the exact PATH. Leading hypothesis is their node `spawnSync` env ending up with both `Path` and `PATH`, which can let `where.exe` resolve while cmd's own lookup fails — exactly the shape observed. If it turns out real it is a separate issue and it affects codex and droid too, since they ship the same wrapper.

**Task A (reading the Windows IDE build) is blocked on their side by their own permission classifier.** I told them to drop it and not ask their user — I'm extracting the installer here instead; it is Inno Setup 6.4, which needs a newer innoextract than the released one, building now. If it fails I'll say the Windows IDE build is unread and lean on what I have: the shipped Windows *CLI* package, plus three IDE builds whose composed string is byte-identical with the win32 branch present unfolded.

Full-tree lint and the whole unit suite are running now. I have not committed or pushed — that needs my user, so I'll put the branch and PR to them once the suite is clean.

Cursor runs `.cursor/hooks.json` commands on Windows through PowerShell, **not** cmd.exe — read out of the shipped bundles 2026-09-10 (cursor-agent CLI windows/x64 2026.09.08-6caf4ff; Cursor IDE 3.19.13, 3.15.19, 3.11.19). Composition, byte-identical across all four builds:

`spawn(<pwsh|powershell|%SYSTEMROOT%\System32\WindowsPowerShell\v1.0\powershell.exe>, [-NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass (IDE only), "-c", SCRIPT])` where SCRIPT is `$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8; Get-Content -LiteralPath '<tmp>\cursor-hook-payload-*.json' -Raw | & { $input | <HOOK_COMMAND> }`. Payload: temp file on Windows, stdin on macOS/Linux (`$SHELL` else `/bin/sh -c`). Both Windows runners (native CLI and IDE) read the same project file, so one wrapper must serve both — it does.

**Consequence:** the `sh -c '…'` wrapper survives PowerShell's parse (single quotes are literal), so the droid-style cmd.exe quote mangling does NOT apply. It fails because `sh` does not resolve in the PowerShell child: Git for Windows puts `sh.exe` in `…\Git\usr\bin` and `…\Git\bin`, neither on the machine PATH (only `…\Git\cmd`), while `UseWindowsProductionHooks` probes with the `entire enable` process's PATH — and MSYS translates PATH for native children, so a probe from Git Bash sees `sh` when Cursor does not. Same gate fix as droid ([[project_droid_windows_hooks_cmd_exe]]), different mechanism: a probe of the wrong process's environment, which no stronger probe command fixes. Switching wrapper moves the dependency to `entire` being on the child's PATH.

**Getting the builds** (see [[reference_agent_binary_inspection]]): native Windows CLI is real — `irm 'https://cursor.com/install?win32=true' | iex`, package at `https://downloads.cursor.com/lab/<ver>/windows/<arch>/agent-cli-package.zip` (**.zip**; a `.tar.gz` probe 403s and reads as "no Windows CLI"), installs to `%LOCALAPPDATA%\cursor-agent\versions\`. The CLI bundle IS platform-folded (`getCommandHookPayloadTransportMode()` → `stdin` vs `windows_temp_file`), so the mac build answers wrongly; the IDE bundle is not folded (`_getBackendOS()===1` is Windows). Stable across versions back to 3.11.19 — no droid-style composition churn.

Cursor-side bug, not ours: the Windows CLI picks a **bash** executor whenever `MSYSTEM` is set, before considering PowerShell, while still composing the PowerShell script — so `cursor-agent` started from Git Bash feeds that script to `bash -c` and hooks are dead there whatever we install. IDE unaffected.

---
name: powershell-stdin-bom
description: "Windows PowerShell 5.1 prepends a UTF-8 BOM when piping to a native command; Go's json.Decoder rejects it, breaking agent hook input"
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Windows PowerShell **5.1** writes a UTF-8 BOM ahead of the bytes when it pipes
pipeline output to a native command's stdin, and Go's `json.NewDecoder` does not
skip a BOM — it fails as `invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value`.
Diagnose any "hook input" parse failure on Windows by hex-dumping the first
bytes (`ef bb bf`) before suspecting the payload.

Measured on Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1 (2026-09-10), 50-byte UTF-8 payload,
varying console codepage against the presence of an
`$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` line:

| codepage | `$OutputEncoding` set | bytes | head |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1252 | yes | 55 | `ef bb bf 7b …` |
| 1252 | no | 52 | `7b …` |
| 65001 | yes | 58 | `ef bb bf ef bb bf 7b …` |
| 65001 | no | 55 | `ef bb bf 7b …` |

Two **independent** producers that stack, so a strip-once fix is not enough:
the `$OutputEncoding` assignment (any codepage), and a UTF-8 console codepage
via `[Console]::OutputEncoding`. 5.1's default `$OutputEncoding` is
`ASCIIEncoding` (preamble 0), which is why callers set it at all;
`[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8` is the BOM-carrying encoder and
`New-Object System.Text.UTF8Encoding($false)` is the BOM-less one. PowerShell
also appends a trailing CRLF, which a streaming JSON decoder ignores.

This is how Cursor's hooks break on Windows — see
[[cursor-windows-hooks-powershell]] for the composition. It is
wrapper-independent: `sh -c`, `cmd.exe /c` and a bare invocation all deliver
correct argv and all three deliver a BOM-prefixed payload. pwsh (7.x) is
expected not to emit the preamble, unverified.

input.message:
Both open items closed. Case 5 is an instrument artifact — Cursor's env is a straight pass-through — and I got the Windows IDE build read after all, so nothing in the PR has to be hedged.

**Cursor's hook env cannot produce the duplicate-key condition.** Read out of the extracted Windows build, the spawn env is `{...process.env, ...{TERM:"dumb",NO_COLOR:"1",FORCE_COLOR:"0",_ZO_DOCTOR:"0"}, ...{CURSOR_AGENT:"1",COMPOSER_NO_INTERACTION:"1"}, ...perCall}`, and the per-call object (`_buildHookEnvironment`, renderer side) returns only `CURSOR_PROJECT_DIR`, `CURSOR_VERSION`, `CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` and optional `CURSOR_CODE_REMOTE` / `CURSOR_USER_EMAIL` / `CURSOR_TRANSCRIPT_PATH`. No PATH-ish key at any layer, so `process.env`'s single casing survives and `where.exe` and cmd resolve against the same value. So the guard is not reachable in the field through Cursor, and given their `Start-Process` false negative earlier I'm treating case 5 as their node harness. I've still asked for the intermediate `errorlevel`; if it comes back 0 that confirms the two-lookup reading, and either way it is not a blocker.

One residual, not worth chasing: a `sessionStart` hook may *return* an `env` which Cursor merges into later hooks' environment, so a hook author could inject a differently-cased PATH themselves. Self-inflicted, and not ours.

Half right, and the distinction matters: UTF-8 itself is everywhere — it's the *BOM* that's a Windows habit. On the substance you're right that the only producer we've measured is Windows PowerShell, and every caller of that function reads a payload written by an agent on the same machine, so `runtime.GOOS == "windows"` would cover every case we know about. I'd still not gate it, for one practical reason:

**Our test suite runs on Linux and macOS.** Gated on GOOS, the skip never executes in the normal `go test` job, and the Windows job filters to `-run '(Windows|MSYS)'`, which my test names don't match — so the fix would ship with tests that never exercise it on any runner. Ungated, the same tests prove the behaviour everywhere, and the Windows path is then the same code everyone else ran.

Secondary, but it's why ungating isn't a compromise: tolerating a leading BOM is what most JSON readers do — RFC 8259 explicitly permits ignoring one — and Go's decoder is the unusually strict one. Since a BOM is never legal JSON, skipping it can only turn a hard failure into a success; there's no input it makes worse. So it reads as "be normal about BOMs" rather than "special-case Windows".

On putting it in the same PR — your call and I'll do it, but the cost is that #2349 is blocked on an approval and a CodeQL settings conflict none of us can clear, and the BOM fix is the one that actually helps a Windows Cursor user *today* (it's wrapper-independent — sh, cmd and bare all delivered a BOM-prefixed payload). Bundled, it waits on that. It's also the wider blast radius of the two: one chokepoint every agent and the plugin boundary passes through, versus cursor's `InstallHooks`.

hooks: tolerate a UTF-8 BOM on hook input

Cursor's Windows hook runner pipes the JSON payload through PowerShell,
prefixing the command with `$OutputEncoding =
[System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8`. Under Windows PowerShell 5.1 that encoder
carries a 3-byte preamble, so the payload reaches the hook with a leading
BOM and `json.NewDecoder` — which does not skip one — fails:

    failed to parse hook input: invalid character 'ï' looking for beginning of value

Measured on Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1 against the shipped entire.exe,
which produced exactly that error. Isolating the producers with a 50-byte
payload: the `$OutputEncoding` line adds one BOM at any console codepage,
and a UTF-8 console codepage adds a second, independently — so they stack
and a single strip is not enough.

skipUTF8BOM sits at ReadHookInputRawLimited, the one decode every agent's
hook read funnels through, so this covers claude-code, copilot-cli and the
external-plugin boundary as well as cursor. It is wrapper-independent:
sh -c, cmd.exe /c and a bare invocation all deliver a BOM-prefixed
payload, so no wrapper change fixes this.

Each strip is gated on a one-byte peek. Peek(3) blocks until three bytes
arrive, so peeking three unconditionally would hang on a short-but-valid
payload written into a pipe that stays open — issue #1398 again. The new
`shorter than a BOM` case fails with exactly that hang when the gate is
removed.

cursor: install the cmd.exe hook wrappers on Windows

Cursor's Windows hook runner is PowerShell, not cmd.exe, and the sh
wrapper it installs today cannot run there. Issue #1424 reported it
(Windows 11 + Git Bash, nothing recorded); #1735 fixed two of that
report's three causes and left this one behind a probe, and the retest it
asked for was never posted.

Read out of the shipped per-platform builds — Cursor IDE 3.19.19
win32/x64, extracted from the installer, and the native cursor-agent CLI
windows/x64 2026.09.08-6caf4ff — every hook command is spawned as:

    <pwsh|powershell> [-NoProfile -NonInteractive -ExecutionPolicy Bypass]
      -c "$OutputEncoding = [System.Text.Encoding]::UTF8;
          Get-Content -LiteralPath '<tmp>\cursor-hook-payload-*.json' -Raw
          | & { $input | <command> }"

with the stored command inserted verbatim. Both Windows runners read the
same .cursor/hooks.json and compose that identically, as do IDE 3.15.19
and 3.11.19 — no composition churn to track. Reading per platform was
necessary: the CLI bundle folds its platform branch, so the macOS build
answers this question wrongly.

So the sh wrapper is not mangled the way droid's is — PowerShell single
quotes are literal and the script reaches sh as one argument. It fails
because `sh` must resolve in the PATH of the PowerShell child Cursor
spawns, while UseWindowsProductionHooks probes for sh in the `entire
enable` process. Git for Windows installs sh.exe under ...\Git\usr\bin and
...\Git\bin, neither on the machine PATH (only ...\Git\cmd is), and MSYS
translates PATH for native children — so `entire enable` from Git Bash
passes the probe and writes a wrapper Cursor cannot run. That is #1424's
environment exactly, and no stronger probe command fixes it, because the
probe measures the wrong process. Hence agent.HookHostIsWindows.

The failure is invisible rather than swallowed: a CommandNotFoundException
inside `& { $input | ... }` does not set powershell.exe's exit code, so
Cursor sees exit 0. Measured on Windows 11 / PowerShell 5.1; the same
command standalone exits 1.

This moves the PATH dependency rather than removing it, from `sh` on the
child's PATH — which Git for Windows' default install does not satisfy —
to `entire` on it, which every documented install method does. When
`entire` is genuinely unreachable all three wrapper shapes exit 0 and do
nothing.

Migration needs no new code: syncEntireHook already replaces a managed
hook whose command is not the wanted one, and IsManagedHookCommand
recognises both Windows shapes. TestInstallHooks_WindowsMigratesShWrappers
pins it, per hook type, since two entries double-fire.

Tests: the two probe tests are replaced by one that drives the probe BOTH
ways and asserts the cmd wrappers either way, because the probe's answer
must no longer matter; the flip test becomes an sh->cmd migration test
seeded by installing as a non-Windows host. Thirteen assertions hardcoded
the sh wrapper and would have failed on a Windows host, where CI's
-run '(Windows|MSYS)' filter would not have caught them; they are now
keyed to the host, with cursorWindowsHookCommand kept non-delegating so
something still pins the command prefix and every verb.
TestCommittedDogfoodHooksIsCurrent skips on Windows: the committed file
can only carry one form, and it carries the sh one, which is right for
this repo's own CI.

TestWindowsWrappers_CursorComposition executes the wrappers through the
composition above on a real Windows runner, including that the payload
reaches the wrapped command's stdin — the property codex's and droid's
runners have no equivalent of — and that the sh wrapper with no reachable
sh runs nothing and still exits 0.

Not fixed by any wrapper, and Cursor's to fix: the cursor-agent CLI picks
a bash shell executor whenever MSYSTEM is set, i.e. started from Git Bash,
while still composing the PowerShell script above, so hooks cannot run
there at all. The IDE is unaffected, so #1424's reporter is not.

Cursor implements no HookFreshness, so `entire status` and `doctor` will
not report the stale sh wrapper and AreHooksInstalled still answers true
for it: an already-enabled Windows repo keeps broken hooks until someone
re-runs `entire enable`. A HookFreshness for cursor is the durable fix and
is not in this change.

Both commits are in. Here they are:

```
8ab5086ba cursor: install the cmd.exe hook wrappers on Windows
71eef52fc hooks: tolerate a UTF-8 BOM on hook input
d99ea12c0 factoryai-droid: lift the hook-command wrappers out of InstallHooks   <- #2349's tip
```

Branch is `fix-cursor-ai-windows-test`, rebased onto `fix-droid-ai-windows-test`, so both Windows fixes are in the one PR as you wanted.

**What the cursor commit does** — four files:
- `cursor/hooks.go`: `UseWindowsProductionHooks(ctx)` → `HookHostIsWindows()`, with the seven wrapper constructions lifted into `silentHookCommand` the way droid's commit did it (same maintidx reason, and the explanation lands where it belongs).
- `agent/hook_command.go`: `HookHostIsWindows`'s doc now carries both mechanisms — the shell mangling the wrapper (droid) and the wrapper's dependency being unreachable where the hook runs (cursor) — instead of saying cursor's case is unknown.
- `cursor/hooks_test.go`: the two probe tests collapse into one that drives the probe *both* ways and asserts cmd wrappers either way, since the probe's answer must no longer matter; the flip test becomes an sh→cmd migration test with per-type counts; 13 hardcoded sh assertions host-keyed, keeping `cursorWindowsHookCommand` non-delegating so something still pins the prefix and every verb; dogfood test skips on Windows.
- `agent/hook_command_exec_windows_test.go`: `runCursorWrapper` models the PowerShell composition and asserts the payload reaches the wrapped command's **stdin** — which codex's and droid's runners never check — plus a subtest showing the sh wrapper with no reachable `sh` runs nothing and still exits 0.

**Both new tests are load-bearing**: putting the old gate back fails `…WhateverTheProbeSays/sh_runs_in_this_process` and `…WindowsMigratesShWrappers`, and they pass on the new one. Same check I did for the BOM gate.

Agent tree lint 0 issues; full-tree lint and the whole unit suite are running now.

Two things I could not verify from here: `TestWindowsWrappers_CursorComposition` is Windows-only, so it first runs in CI's Windows job (it matches the `(Windows|MSYS)` filter deliberately) — `GOOS=windows go vet` is all I could do locally. And I deliberately left out an exit-code-propagation subtest, since I haven't measured whether PowerShell propagates a native exit code out of `& { … }`.

Still not pushed. Say the word and I'll push and open the PR against `fix-droid-ai-windows-test`.
